turn1.explanation: The unit fires on the last token of a line, the position just before a newline, regardless of what kind of token sits there (a value, brace, punctuation, word or name piece) or what kind of text it is.
turn1.evidence: Every top example is marked at a line end: YAML values ('1', '0', '15'), license-header line ends ('software', ','), opening '{' after method or CSS selector lines, 'Book' and '.' before paragraph breaks, and docblock line ends ('ME', 'uk', 'am', '"'). Middle examples follow the same pattern with surname fragments in result lists, '}' after headings, 'Invention' and list-item periods, all at line ends; mid-line tokens stay unmarked.
turn1.missing_data: Per-token activations across whole documents, to confirm that mid-line tokens stay near zero and to check whether wrapped or long lines without a newline still fire.
